questions.question: Before a trip, you should make sure that:

options.text: The brake pedal sticks.
The gas pedal is loose.
The pedal surfaces have grooves and are not smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pedal surfaces have grooves and are not smooth.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle's pedals before driving. Make sure nothing blocks the pedals. The pedal surfaces should have grooves so your feet do not slip.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, a driver should:

options.text: Jump directly from the seat to the ground.
Keep at least one hand on the vehicle.
Face toward the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face toward the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When leaving a vehicle during a skills test, always face the vehicle and hold onto it with three points of contact. If driving a bus, use the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may cause you to fail the skills test.

questions.question: When boarding a school bus, students should:

options.text: Walk in a single line, one after another.
Walk in pairs.
Not use the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk in a single line, one after another.
questions.explanation: Students should board the bus slowly and in a single line. They should always use the handrail for safety.

questions.question: During a skills test, a 'look' means:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.
questions.explanation: A look is when you leave your seat, get out, and walk to the back to check your vehicle's position. For straight line backing, you can only do one look. For other exercises, you can do up to two looks.

questions.question: When students are picked up by a school bus:

options.text: Students should wait at an official bus stop.
The driver should pick up students walking to a bus stop.
Parents can decide where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at an official bus stop.
questions.explanation: Bus drivers can only pick up students at official stops approved by the school.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the bus driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Slow down and be careful.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: At a passive railroad crossing, who decides if it is safe to cross:

options.text: The driver.
A control device signals when to go.
The vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: A passive crossing has no traffic signals or control devices. The driver must decide if it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should show:

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the overhead mirror to show the top of the rear window. This lets you see all students on the bus, including those sitting right behind you.

questions.question: During testing exercises (except straight line backing), how many times can a driver exit the vehicle to check its position:

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two times.
questions.explanation: You can exit to check your vehicle's position (called a look) during tests. For straight line backing, you can look only once. For other exercises, you can look up to two times.

questions.question: If a tornado is approaching and there is no nearby shelter, where should students go:

options.text: To a nearby ditch.
To the closest tree.
Near a river.

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby ditch.
questions.explanation: If a tornado approaches and there is no building to shelter in, take students to a nearby ditch or culvert. Avoid areas that could flood and stay far from the bus so it cannot fall on you if it tips.

questions.question: What should happen if a school bus stalls on railroad tracks?

options.text: Students should stay on the bus.
Students should be evacuated to a location near the bus.
Students should be evacuated and moved far away from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should be evacuated and moved far away from the bus.
questions.explanation: If a school bus stalls or gets stuck on railroad tracks, the driver must evacuate everyone immediately. Students should be led far away from the bus at an angle toward the direction of oncoming trains. This protects them from debris if a train hits the bus.

questions.question: If a bus is evacuated, where is the safest place for students to stand?

options.text: No more than 50 feet away from the bus.
Downwind of the bus in case of fire.
Far away from any railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Far away from any railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: After evacuating, students should be led at least 100 feet away from the road, in the direction of oncoming traffic. This keeps them safe from debris if another vehicle hits the bus. They should also be upwind of any fires and as far as possible from railroad tracks.

questions.question: How should you complete a driver's side parallel parking maneuver?

options.text: Drive straight forward into the parking space.
Back up past the parking space, then drive forward into it.
Drive forward past the parking space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: For a parking space on your left, drive past it first. Then back up into the space while moving the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must stay completely within the space lines.

questions.question: How often should pre-trip inspections be done, and in what way?

options.text: Differently each time to focus on different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This routine helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't skip anything.

questions.question: After students get off the bus at school, what should the driver do?

options.text: Not worry about where the students go.
Leave after students enter the school building.
Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for sleeping students.
questions.explanation: After students get off at school, the driver should walk through the bus to check for sleeping or hiding students and items left behind. Students should exit in an orderly way with the driver watching them.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to make a turn during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Don't use a turn signal because you were told to make the turn.
Check traffic only to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, you must check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Which of the following can properly adjusted crossover mirrors NOT show you?

options.text: The right and left front tires touching the ground.
The area in front of the bus.
The tops of the right and left rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tops of the right and left rear tires.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted crossover mirrors show the entire area in front of the bus from the front bumper at ground level to where you can see directly. They also show the right and left front tires touching the ground and the area from the front to the service door. They do not show the tops of the rear tires.

questions.question: During the driving test, what will the examiner score you on?

options.text: Your attitude.
How quickly you reach your destination.
Your overall driving behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your overall driving behavior.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: What does ABS allow you to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Drive less carefully.
Keep control on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control on slippery surfaces.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) prevent the brakes from locking up on slippery surfaces. If you brake hard on a slippery surface, ABS helps you stay in control. Drive a vehicle with ABS the same way as one without it.

questions.question: If the driver must leave a school bus to check if all waiting students have boarded, what should the driver do?

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn off the bus and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the bus and take the key.
questions.explanation: If you need to leave the bus to find a missing student, turn off the engine and take the key. Check around and underneath the bus for the student.
